newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Skoda confirms Brazil truck plant plan.
newsitem.headline: Skoda confirms Brazil truck plant plan.

text.p: Czech truckmaker Skoda confirmed Wednesday it would build a new special truck plant in Brazil's northeastern Bahia state.

Lubomir Soudek, chairman of the Skoda board, told Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the company intended to make an initial investment of $100 million in the plant which would produce between 2,500 and 3,000 trucks a year.
The difficult-terrain trucks would be suitable for use in mining and projects to build roads and hydroelectric dams, Soudek told reporters after meeting with Cardoso.
The plant would be up and running by September 1998 and would most likely be located in the outskirts of Salvador, the capital of Bahia state, he said.

Skoda is set to benefit from special fiscal incentives granted to carmakers located in Brazil's underdeveloped northeast. Several other companies have pledged more than $1.7 billion in investments in the region.

In May, Brazilian government officials said Skoda was also planning another truck plant in the southern state of Santa Catarina capable of producing 5,000 units a year. But Soudek did not mention those plans to reporters Wednesday.
